title: Contract Pricing Agreement Rebate Clawback: Return Frequency Share
content:
# Return frequency and the Contract Pricing Agreement rebate clawback

**Clause.** A rebate clawback for a return on a Contract Pricing Agreement carries a frequency share that follows how many return receipt lines the customer's ship-tos received less than 12 whole months before the handling date, this return included. One such line or none carries a frequency share of 0.5; two to 4 lines carry 0.75; more lines carry a frequency share of 1. The frequency share multiplies the unrounded clawback before the clawback's limit, its floor at 0.00 and its rounding to the cent are applied.

**Records counted.** Every return receipt line recorded on any of the customer's Ship-To Fulfillment Account records counts, one per receipt line, when its receipt date is less than 12 whole months before the handling date. Whole months between two dates are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's day of the month is earlier than the earlier date's. Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest or most recent record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

| Receipt lines in the window | Frequency share |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 0.5 |
| 2, 3 or 4 | 0.75 |
| 5 or more | 1 |

**Window edge (hypothetical dates).** Handled on 10 June: a receipt dated 11 June of the year before is 11 whole months earlier and counts; a receipt dated 10 June of the year before is 12 whole months earlier and does not count.

**Worked case (hypothetical).** Three receipt lines in the window and an unrounded clawback of 8.00: share 0.75, giving 6.00.
